purpose: Local, versioned copy of the RBI and MeitY instruments that can govern a debt-collection voice agent. This is not a dump of either website.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: Commercial banks other than Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks, Regional Rural Banks, and Local Area Banks
sources.why_included: Current recovery-agent conduct rules for commercial banks live in this direction, including the ban on harassment and calls before 8:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: NBFCs, all layers, unless a paragraph says otherwise
sources.why_included: Current NBFC recovery-agent conduct rules, including harassment, calling hours, confidentiality, and authorisation.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Commercial banks other than Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks, Regional Rural Banks, and Local Area Banks
sources.why_included: Replaces the current commercial-bank recovery-agent paragraphs on 1 January 2027. Stored now so the engine can switch on the effective date without going back to the website.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Small Finance Banks
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is a small finance bank.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Local Area Banks
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is a local area bank.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Regional Rural Banks
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is a regional rural bank.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Urban Co-operative Banks
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is an urban co-operative bank.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Rural Co-operative Banks
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is a rural co-operative bank.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions – Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: All India Financial Institutions
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is an all-India financial institution.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: NBFCs, excluding Mortgage Guarantee Companies, Core Investment Companies, NBFC-Account Aggregators, Standalone Primary Dealers, Non-Operating Financial Holding Companies, and NBFCs with no customer interface
sources.why_included: Replaces the current NBFC recovery-agent paragraphs on 1 January 2027.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Housing Finance Companies) Third Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.applicable_entity: Housing Finance Companies
sources.why_included: Parallel recovery-conduct amendment. Applies only when the lender is a housing finance company.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: Digital lending by commercial banks, primary urban co-operative banks, state and central co-operative banks, NBFCs including housing finance companies, and all-India financial institutions
sources.why_included: Requires the lender to tell the borrower who the recovery agent is, by email or SMS, before that agent makes contact. Also binds lending service providers who recover digital loans.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: Commercial banks, for the digital-lending chapter only
sources.why_included: The November 2025 consolidation repeats digital-lending recovery duties inside the credit-facilities direction. Only that chapter is relevant to this agent. The rest of the file is kept so the source stays complete and auditable.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: NBFCs, for the digital-lending chapter only
sources.why_included: NBFC digital-lending recovery duties, including notice of the recovery agent before contact, and the statement that the NBFC remains liable for the lending service provider.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: Scheduled commercial banks, for outsourced recovery and for this voice system as an IT or financial-services service provider
sources.why_included: Confidentiality, customer-data handling, and the rule that outsourcing does not move responsibility off the bank.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: NBFCs, with graded IT-outsourcing duties by layer
sources.why_included: Same confidentiality and responsibility rules when the lender is an NBFC.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Cards and Debit Cards: Issuance and Conduct) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: Commercial banks, only when the debt being collected is a credit card or debit card dues
sources.why_included: Card recovery requires the issuer to give the cardholder the agent's name and contact details on assignment, and limits what customer information the agent may receive.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Cards: Issuance and Conduct) Directions, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: NBFCs, only when the debt being collected is credit card dues
sources.why_included: Same card-recovery limits when the card issuer is an NBFC.

sources.title: RBI Issues Amendment Directions on Conduct of Regulated Entities in Recovery of Loans and Engagement of Recovery Agents
sources.applicable_entity: Index of the nine recovery amendments. Not itself a conduct rule.
sources.why_included: Official list of which recovery amendments were issued, and the shared effective date of 1 January 2027.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
sources.applicable_entity: Anyone processing digital personal data of a borrower in India, including a voice agent and its lender principal
sources.why_included: The Act is the MeitY statute for borrower personal data. Most operative duties are not in force yet. Commencement is fixed by G.S.R. 843(E).

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
sources.applicable_entity: Data fiduciaries and processors under the DPDP Act
sources.why_included: Rules 1, 2 and 17 to 21 took effect on 13 November 2025. Rule 4 takes effect on 13 November 2026. Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 take effect on 13 May 2027.

sources.title: Notification bringing provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 into force
sources.applicable_entity: Determines which DPDP Act sections bind a voice agent on a given date
sources.why_included: Without this notification the Act cannot be applied. Most borrower-facing duties start on 13 May 2027.
